description: T1 preferred over T2 if any of these hold (all from T1's perspective). NL is correct for any preference relation; BNL requires strict partial order.
rules_explained: Rule 1: p1>p2 AND np1<np2 AND union(T1)>=union(T2) => T1 better
Rule 3: p1=p2 AND np1=np2 AND union(T1)>union(T2) => T1 better
Rule 4: p1=p2 AND np1>np2 AND union(T2)>union(T1) => T2 better (from T1's view: T1 dominated)
Rule 5: p1>p2 AND np1=np2 AND union(T1)>union(T2) => T1 better

or._comment: Rule 1: more protected, fewer non-protected, at least as good unionability
Rule 3: same protected, same non-protected, strictly better unionability
Rule 4: same protected, more non-protected, worse unionability => T2 better, so from T1's view: T1 is NOT preferred. Written reversed: T1 has fewer np AND better union means T1 preferred.
Rule 5: more protected, same non-protected, strictly better unionability
